Release years of these Mario games.Donkey Kong (arcade): Mario debuted here as a carpenter called Jumpman, designed by Shigeru Miyamoto, long before he became a plumber.
Nintendo's best-selling NES game for decades, it sold more than 40 million copies and rescued the home console industry after the 1983 crash.
Release years of these Mario games.Super Mario Bros. 3: Introduced the raccoon suit and the Tanooki tail, and the overworld map screen that let players choose their path.
Release years of these Mario games.Super Mario World: Launched alongside the SNES, it introduced Yoshi, the green dinosaur Mario can ride and eat enemies with.
Release years of these Mario games.Super Mario Kart: This racing game used a graphics trick called Mode 7 to rotate the flat track into a pseudo-3D view.
Release years of these Mario games.Super Mario 64: Mario's first 3D adventure launched with the Nintendo 64 and showed off its analog stick, with Mario running around a castle's paintings.
Release years of these Mario games.Super Mario Sunshine: This GameCube game was set on Isle Delfino, with Mario using a water-spraying backpack called FLUDD.
Release years of these Mario games.Super Mario Galaxy: Mario hops across tiny planets with their own gravity, and the Wii game won wide praise for creative level design.
Release years of these Mario games.Super Mario Odyssey: Mario's hat sidekick Cappy lets him capture enemies, and the New Donk City level features Pauline singing Jump Up, Super Star.
Release years of these Mario games.Super Mario Bros. Wonder: Its Wonder Flowers bend levels into surreal gags, and Mario got a new voice actor for the first time in decades.

World literature giants, by birth year.Dante Alighieri: He wrote the Divine Comedy in Tuscan Italian rather than Latin, helping to make it the standard literary Italian, after being exiled from Florence.
World literature giants, by birth year.Miguel de Cervantes: He lost the use of his left hand at the Battle of Lepanto, was held captive in Algiers, and wrote Don Quixote in his late fifties.
World literature giants, by birth year.Johann Wolfgang von Goethe: His Faust took about six decades to finish, and he also wrote on botany and a theory of color.
World literature giants, by birth year.Victor Hugo: His novel Notre-Dame de Paris renewed interest in the cathedral, helping to spark its 19th-century restoration.
World literature giants, by birth year.Fyodor Dostoevsky: Sentenced to death in 1849 and reprieved at the last moment on the scaffold, he spent years in Siberian prison camp.
World literature giants, by birth year.Leo Tolstoy: His wife Sophia hand-copied drafts of War and Peace several times, and he later grew to doubt his own great novels.
World literature giants, by birth year.Franz Kafka: He asked his friend Max Brod to burn his manuscripts, but Brod refused and published The Trial and The Castle.
World literature giants, by birth year.Albert Camus: He won the Nobel Prize at 44, and played as goalkeeper in Algiers, saying football taught him about ethics.
World literature giants, by birth year.Gabriel García Márquez: His novel One Hundred Years of Solitude made magical realism famous worldwide, and he won the Nobel Prize in 1982.
World literature giants, by birth year.Haruki Murakami: He ran a jazz bar in Tokyo, then decided to write a novel while watching a baseball game, and he is a keen marathon runner.

Films scored by John Williams, in order.Jaws: Its two-note motif reportedly unnerved audiences, and Spielberg credited the score for much of the film's success. It won Williams an Oscar.
Films scored by John Williams, in order.Star Wars: Recorded with the London Symphony Orchestra, it won an Oscar and revived grand orchestral scoring in cinema.
Films scored by John Williams, in order.Superman: Its heroic march is one of film music's most recognisable fanfares, matched to the tagline 'You'll believe a man can fly'.
Films scored by John Williams, in order.Raiders of the Lost Ark: The Raiders March was written for a hero who debuted in this film, and the score earned an Oscar nomination.
Films scored by John Williams, in order.E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial: Spielberg famously re-edited the film's chase finale to match Williams's music, and the score won an Oscar.
Films scored by John Williams, in order.Home Alone: Includes the song 'Somewhere in My Memory', and the score and song both earned Oscar nominations.
Films scored by John Williams, in order.Jurassic Park: Its soaring main theme is one of Williams's best known, and the film pioneered realistic computer-made dinosaurs.
Films scored by John Williams, in order.Saving Private Ryan: His 'Hymn to the Fallen' gives the film's war scenes a solemn, restrained voice, and the score earned an Oscar nomination.
Films scored by John Williams, in order.Harry Potter (first film): 'Hedwig's Theme' opens with a celesta and became the series' musical signature, reused in all eight films.
Films scored by John Williams, in order.Lincoln: Spielberg's drama with Daniel Day-Lewis earned Williams another Oscar nomination for a subdued, hymn-like score.

TV comedy premieres of the 2000s and bey.Malcolm in the Middle: Frankie Muniz played a genius kid, and Bryan Cranston played his dad Hal, years before Breaking Bad.
TV comedy premieres of the 2000s and bey.Scrubs: Bill Lawrence's hospital comedy ran nine seasons and was praised by real doctors for its accuracy about medical life.
TV comedy premieres of the 2000s and bey.Arrested Development: Narrated by Ron Howard, it was cancelled in 2006 after three seasons and revived by Netflix in 2013.
TV comedy premieres of the 2000s and bey.30 Rock: Created by Tina Fey from her SNL years, it won the Emmy for Outstanding Comedy Series three years in a row.
TV comedy premieres of the 2000s and bey.Parks and Recreation: Set in fictional Pawnee, Indiana, it spawned lasting fan favourites like Li'l Sebastian the miniature horse.
TV comedy premieres of the 2000s and bey.New Girl: Zooey Deschanel's quirky Jess lived with three men, and the show gave us the 'True American' drinking game.
TV comedy premieres of the 2000s and bey.Brooklyn Nine-Nine: Fox cancelled it in 2018, then NBC picked it up within about a day after fans' outcry.
TV comedy premieres of the 2000s and bey.Schitt's Creek: Created by Dan and Eugene Levy, it swept the main comedy Emmys in 2020, the first show to win all seven major comedy awards.
TV comedy premieres of the 2000s and bey.Ted Lasso: It began as promo sketches for NBC Sports' Premier League coverage in 2013, starring Jason Sudeikis.
TV comedy premieres of the 2000s and bey.Abbott Elementary: Quinta Brunson's mockumentary about a Philadelphia public school was inspired by her mother, a teacher.

Ancient China, in chronological order.Oracle bone inscriptions: Shang diviners carved questions onto turtle shells and ox bones, then heated them. It's the earliest Chinese writing.
Ancient China, in chronological order.Confucius born: Born in the state of Lu, his teachings were recorded by students in the Analects.
Ancient China, in chronological order.Qin unifies China: Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor, standardised writing and weights, and was buried with the Terracotta Army.
Ancient China, in chronological order.Sima Qian finishes his history: He wrote Records of the Grand Historian after being castrated as punishment for defending a general.
Ancient China, in chronological order.White Horse Temple founded: Tradition says it was China's first Buddhist temple, at Luoyang, founded for two monks from India.
Ancient China, in chronological order.Three Kingdoms era begins: Wei, Shu and Wu fought for power, a period dramatised in the novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms.
Ancient China, in chronological order.Sui Grand Canal completed: This canal linked the Yellow and Yangtze rivers, and became part of the world's longest artificial waterway, over 1,700 km.
Ancient China, in chronological order.Diamond Sutra printed: The oldest dated printed book, it was found in the Dunhuang caves and now sits in the British Library.
Ancient China, in chronological order.Song capital moves to Hangzhou: After the north fell to the Jurchens, the Southern Song made Hangzhou its capital, and it became one of the world's largest cities.
Ancient China, in chronological order.Forbidden City completed: The palace in Beijing housed 24 emperors from the Ming and Qing dynasties.

The Ruy Lopez, Closed: move by move.e4: The most popular first move, it opens lines for the queen and a bishop and fights for the center.
The Ruy Lopez, Closed: move by move.e5: Black mirrors White's move, a classical response that stakes a claim to the center.
The Ruy Lopez, Closed: move by move.Nf3: It develops a knight and attacks Black's e5 pawn at the same time.
The Ruy Lopez, Closed: move by move.Nc6: This move defends the e5 pawn and brings out the other knight.
The Ruy Lopez, Closed: move by move.Bb5: The Ruy Lopez is named for a 16th-century Spanish priest, Ruy López de Segura, who analyzed this move in his 1561 book.
The Ruy Lopez, Closed: move by move.a6: Called the Morphy Defense after the American Paul Morphy, it asks White's bishop what it intends to do.
The Ruy Lopez, Closed: move by move.Ba4: White keeps the pin tension going rather than trading, since after Bxc6 dxc6 Black gets the bishop pair.
The Ruy Lopez, Closed: move by move.Nf6: This develops a knight and hits White's e4 pawn.
The Ruy Lopez, Closed: move by move.O-O: Castling is the only move that moves two pieces at once, and White lets the e4 pawn hang as bait.
The Ruy Lopez, Closed: move by move.Be7: This defends the e5 pawn and prepares to castle, steering the game into the Closed Spanish, a main line for over a century.

When these fast-food favorites debuted.Whopper: Introduced at 37 cents, the burger is Burger King's flagship, and the name was chosen to suggest something big.
When these fast-food favorites debuted.Filet-O-Fish: It was created by franchisee Lou Groen for Catholic customers who avoided meat on Fridays, and it beat a ham-and-pineapple rival in a taste test.
When these fast-food favorites debuted.Big Mac: It was created by franchisee Jim Delligatti in Pittsburgh, and the jingle listing its ingredients became famous in 1974.
When these fast-food favorites debuted.Egg McMuffin: Herb Peterson created it in Santa Barbara, using a Teflon ring to cook the egg, and Ray Kroc approved the idea.
When these fast-food favorites debuted.Happy Meal: It debuted in 1979 with a circus wagon theme, after a Guatemalan-born ad man's idea for children's meals.
When these fast-food favorites debuted.Chicken McNuggets: Chef René Arend developed them, and they became a hit once the company dropped the idea of a smaller chicken sandwich.
When these fast-food favorites debuted.McFlurry (US): The soft-serve dessert was invented in Canada, by a franchisee in Bathurst, New Brunswick, and reached the US in 1997.
When these fast-food favorites debuted.Crunchwrap Supreme: Taco Bell's hexagonal folded tortilla holds a tostada inside for crunch, and is designed to be eaten with one hand.
When these fast-food favorites debuted.Doritos Locos Tacos: The shell is flavoured like Nacho Cheese Doritos, and Taco Bell reported over a billion sold within about a year of launch.
When these fast-food favorites debuted.Impossible Whopper: Its plant-based patty from Impossible Foods gets its meaty flavour from soy leghemoglobin, a plant form of heme.

Speed of sound through each material.Sulfur hexafluoride gas: Sulfur hexafluoride is a very dense gas, so sound travels through it slowly and voices pitched down deep, the opposite of the helium effect.
Speed of sound through each material.Carbon dioxide: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air, and sound travels more slowly through it, which is a fun effect with fizzy drink gas.
Speed of sound through each material.Air: At 20 degrees Celsius sound travels about 343 metres per second in air, and it moves faster when the air warms up.
Speed of sound through each material.Helium gas: Inhaling helium makes your voice squeaky because sound waves travel about three times faster through it, lifting the resonant pitch.
Speed of sound through each material.Hydrogen gas: Hydrogen is the lightest gas, so sound races through it, faster than in any other gas at ordinary temperatures.
Speed of sound through each material.Water: Whales and dolphins exploit that sound moves over four times faster in water than air, and their calls can carry for many kilometres.
Speed of sound through each material.Gold: Gold is soft and dense, and sound still moves through it roughly nine times faster than through air.
Speed of sound through each material.Copper: Copper wire carries sound waves fast, and the same stiffness is why copper pipes ring loudly when tapped.
Speed of sound through each material.Aluminium: Aluminium is light and stiff, and its high sound speed is why tapping an aluminium bar produces a long, clear ringing tone.
Speed of sound through each material.Diamond: Diamond is the stiffest common material, which is why sound races through it, and it is also why it transfers heat so well.

Infamous wildfires, in order.Great Miramichi Fire: This 1825 New Brunswick blaze burned roughly 1.5 million hectares of forest and killed an estimated 160 or more people, one of North America's biggest.
Infamous wildfires, in order.Peshtigo Fire: It hit Wisconsin on the same night as the Great Chicago Fire, yet killed over 1,000 people, making it the deadliest wildfire in US history.
Infamous wildfires, in order.The Big Burn (US Northwest): Fires in Idaho and Montana scorched about 3 million acres in two days, and the disaster shaped the young US Forest Service's policy of fighting every fire.
Infamous wildfires, in order.Ash Wednesday fires: On 16 February 1983, drought and hot, dry winds drove fires across Victoria and South Australia, killing 75 people and destroying thousands of homes.
Infamous wildfires, in order.Yellowstone fires: These fires burned about a third of the park. Scientists later saw them as a natural reset, and lodgepole pine seedlings sprouted thickly within a few years.
Infamous wildfires, in order.Black Saturday: On 7 February 2009, fires during a record heatwave killed 173 people in Victoria, making it Australia's deadliest bushfire day.
Infamous wildfires, in order.Fort McMurray fire: In 2016 this Alberta oil-sands city saw about 88,000 people flee, then the largest wildfire evacuation in Canadian history, and roughly 2,400 buildings burned.
Infamous wildfires, in order.Camp Fire (Paradise): It destroyed the town of Paradise, California, and killed 85 people, making it the deadliest wildfire in the state's history.
Infamous wildfires, in order.Australia's Black Summer: This season burned more than 18 million hectares, an area about the size of Syria, and its smoke plumes circled the globe.
Infamous wildfires, in order.Lahaina fire: Wind-driven flames wiped out the historic Maui town in August 2023, killing at least 100 people, the deadliest US wildfire in over a century.

Euro and US coins by diameter.1 euro cent: Euro cent coins are steel coated with copper, so a magnet can pick them up.
Euro and US coins by diameter.US dime: It is the smallest in size and the thinnest US coin, though worth more than a penny or a nickel.
Euro and US coins by diameter.10 euro cents: It is made of an alloy called Nordic gold, which contains no nickel.
Euro and US coins by diameter.US nickel: It carries Jefferson's home, Monticello, on the back.
Euro and US coins by diameter.20 euro cents: Its scalloped, Spanish flower edge helps visually impaired people tell it apart.
Euro and US coins by diameter.1 euro: It has a bimetallic design, and each country puts its own design on the national side.
Euro and US coins by diameter.US quarter: The 50 State Quarters program between 1999 and 2008 gave each state its own design.
Euro and US coins by diameter.2 euros: The edge carries inscriptions that differ by country.
Euro and US coins by diameter.US dollar coin: The Susan B. Anthony coin was the first with a woman on circulating US currency, but it was often confused with the quarter.
Euro and US coins by diameter.US half dollar: It was introduced after the 1963 assassination of President Kennedy, whose portrait it bears.

Travel businesses, by founding year.Thomas Cook: Thomas Cook organized a rail excursion for temperance campaigners in 1841; the firm's 2019 collapse sparked a huge UK repatriation effort.
Travel businesses, by founding year.American Express: American Express began as an express-mail firm, and it introduced travellers cheques in 1891.
Travel businesses, by founding year.Michelin Guide: A tyre company produced this free guide to get drivers touring, and the famous star ratings arrived in the 1920s.
Travel businesses, by founding year.Club Med: Gérard Blitz founded it with a village of tents on Mallorca, offering simple all-inclusive holidays.
Travel businesses, by founding year.Royal Caribbean: It was founded by Norwegian shipping firms, and its Oasis-class ships carry more than 5,000 guests.
Travel businesses, by founding year.Lonely Planet: Tony and Maureen Wheeler wrote Across Asia on the Cheap at their kitchen table after an overland trip.
Travel businesses, by founding year.Expedia: It began as a Microsoft division before being spun off in 1999, and it became one of the world's largest travel sites.
Travel businesses, by founding year.Tripadvisor: It began as a site collecting guidebook reviews before shifting to travellers' own reviews.
Travel businesses, by founding year.Kayak: The search-comparison site founded by Paul English and Steve Hafner was sold to Priceline for about $1.8 billion in 2013.
Travel businesses, by founding year.Hopper: Started in Montreal, it became known for predicting when flight prices would rise or fall.

Small worlds by average distance from th.Vesta: The second most massive asteroid was visited by NASA's Dawn spacecraft in 2011 and 2012, and it is sometimes visible to the naked eye.
Small worlds by average distance from th.Ceres: This dwarf planet holds about a third of the asteroid belt's mass, and bright salt deposits gleam in its Occator crater.
Small worlds by average distance from th.Hygiea: The fourth-largest asteroid, it is nearly round, so it might qualify as a dwarf planet.
Small worlds by average distance from th.Patroclus (Jupiter trojan): This twin pair of Trojan asteroids is a target for NASA's Lucy mission, which will fly by in 2033.
Small worlds by average distance from th.Chiron: Discovered in 1977 as the first centaur, it behaves as both an asteroid and a comet.
Small worlds by average distance from th.Pluto: Clyde Tombaugh discovered it in 1930, New Horizons flew by in 2015, and it was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
Small worlds by average distance from th.Haumea: This egg-shaped dwarf planet spins in about four hours, and it has two moons and a ring.
Small worlds by average distance from th.Makemake: Named for the Rapa Nui creator god, it was discovered around Easter 2005, and it's one of the brightest objects past Neptune.
Small worlds by average distance from th.Eris: Discovered in 2005, it is more massive than Pluto, and its discovery led to Pluto's reclassification.
Small worlds by average distance from th.Sedna: Its orbit takes around 11,000 years; it was named after the Inuit goddess of the sea.

Sports movies by release.Raging Bull: Robert De Niro gained about 60 pounds to play the older Jake LaMotta and won the Best Actor Oscar.
Sports movies by release.Hoosiers: It is based on Milan High School's 1954 run to the Indiana state title, when a tiny school beat much bigger ones.
Sports movies by release.Field of Dreams: It was filmed on an Iowa farm, and the baseball field still stands in Dyersville.
Sports movies by release.A League of Their Own: It was inspired by the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League, and 'There's no crying in baseball' became famous.
Sports movies by release.Cool Runnings: It was inspired by the Jamaican bobsled team at the 1988 Calgary Winter Olympics.
Sports movies by release.Space Jam: Michael Jordan teams up with the Looney Tunes, and the film's 1996 website is still online.
Sports movies by release.Remember the Titans: Based on the 1971 T. C. Williams High School football team in Alexandria, Virginia.
Sports movies by release.Million Dollar Baby: Clint Eastwood's boxing drama won Best Picture, Best Director and Hilary Swank's Best Actress.
Sports movies by release.Moneyball: Based on Michael Lewis's book about the Oakland A's, who used statistics under manager Billy Beane.
Sports movies by release.Ford v Ferrari: It depicts Ford's push to beat Ferrari at Le Mans in 1966, with Christian Bale as driver Ken Miles.

The cranial nerves, by number.Olfactory: It is the only sense that reaches the cortex without first passing through the thalamus.
The cranial nerves, by number.Optic: Each optic nerve carries about a million fibres, and it is really an extension of the brain.
The cranial nerves, by number.Oculomotor: It moves most of the eye muscles, raises the eyelid and constricts the pupil.
The cranial nerves, by number.Trochlear: The thinnest cranial nerve is the only one to emerge from the back of the brainstem.
The cranial nerves, by number.Trigeminal: The biggest cranial nerve has three branches, and trigeminal neuralgia causes severe facial pain.
The cranial nerves, by number.Abducens: It moves the eye outward, and its long path makes it vulnerable to pressure.
The cranial nerves, by number.Facial: It controls expressions and carries taste from the front of the tongue; Bell's palsy affects it.
The cranial nerves, by number.Vestibulocochlear: It carries hearing and balance from the inner ear to the brain, and it was formerly called the auditory nerve.
The cranial nerves, by number.Glossopharyngeal: Its name means 'tongue and throat'; it carries taste from the back of the tongue and triggers the gag reflex.
The cranial nerves, by number.Vagus: Its Latin name means 'wandering', since it travels from the brainstem into the abdomen.

Calories in each of these.A stalk of celery: Eating celery does take energy to digest, but nowhere near as much as it provides, so the negative calorie idea is a myth.
Calories in each of these.Cup of air-popped popcorn: The kernels pop when the water inside turns to steam at about 180 degrees Celsius, so the hull bursts open and turns inside out.
Calories in each of these.Large egg: Most of the calories are in the yolk, while the white is mostly protein and water, with only about 17 calories.
Calories in each of these.Medium banana: A banana is slightly radioactive because of potassium-40, so scientists jokingly measure small doses in banana equivalents.
Calories in each of these.Can of Coca-Cola: Coca-Cola originally contained extracts of the coca leaf and the kola nut, which gave the drink its name.
Calories in each of these.Whole avocado: Botanically it is a large berry with one seed, and it is also unusually high in fat compared with most fruits.
Calories in each of these.Big Mac: Created in 1967 by Jim Delligatti, a McDonald's franchisee in Pittsburgh, and the Big Mac Index even compares currencies around the world.
Calories in each of these.Stick of butter (113 g): Butter is roughly 80 percent fat, and the rest is mainly water, which is why it spatters when it is heated in a pan.
Calories in each of these.Cup of olive oil: Fat has about nine calories a gram, more than twice that of protein or carbohydrate, so oil is the densest everyday food.
Calories in each of these.400 g jar of Nutella: Made in Alba, Italy by Ferrero, its first ingredient is sugar, and it began in wartime when hazelnuts stretched scarce cocoa.

How many people were aboard.Apollo 11: Collins stayed in orbit alone, and on each pass behind the Moon he was out of radio contact with every other human being.
How many people were aboard.Kon-Tiki raft: Thor Heyerdahl's balsa raft drifted from Peru to Polynesia in 1947, in order to show it could be done with ancient technology; a parrot came too.
How many people were aboard.Shackleton's Endurance: Their ship was crushed by pack ice in 1915, yet all 28 men survived nearly two years in Antarctica, a famous feat of leadership.
How many people were aboard.HMS Bounty at the mutiny: The mutiny of 1789 was led by Fletcher Christian; Captain Bligh then sailed a small open boat over 6,000 kilometres to Timor.
How many people were aboard.Mayflower: A baby, Oceanus Hopkins, was born during the 1620 crossing; the ship also carried livestock and was originally meant to head for Virginia.
How many people were aboard.Mary Rose when it sank: Henry VIII's flagship sank in the Solent in 1545 in sight of the shore, and when raised in 1982 it held a trove of Tudor life.
How many people were aboard.HMS Victory at Trafalgar: Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar in 1805 is still in commission, the oldest warship in the world with that status, in Portsmouth.
How many people were aboard.Lusitania, final voyage: Sunk by a German U-boat off Ireland in 1915, she went down in about 18 minutes, killing nearly 1,200 and stirring American opinion.
How many people were aboard.Titanic, maiden voyage: Her lifeboats could carry little over half of those aboard when she struck an iceberg in April 1912, a flaw behind new safety rules.
How many people were aboard.Wilhelm Gustloff: Torpedoed by a Soviet submarine in January 1945 while carrying refugees and military personnel; it is often named the deadliest sinking in history.

Ways of seeing inside the body, by debut.X-ray: Wilhelm Röntgen found them by accident and X-rayed his wife's hand, calling them X-rays because he did not know what they were.
Ways of seeing inside the body, by debut.ECG: Willem Einthoven's string galvanometer recorded the heart's electrical activity, and he later won a Nobel Prize for it.
Ways of seeing inside the body, by debut.EEG: Hans Berger recorded the first human brain waves in Jena, finding rhythms now called alpha waves, or Berger waves.
Ways of seeing inside the body, by debut.Cerebral angiography: Portuguese neurologist Egas Moniz injected dye to reveal brain blood vessels, and also won a Nobel Prize for the lobotomy.
Ways of seeing inside the body, by debut.Obstetric ultrasound: Glasgow doctor Ian Donald adapted sonar-style flaw detection used in industry to look at unborn babies.
Ways of seeing inside the body, by debut.CT scan: Godfrey Hounsfield built the first at EMI, a company whose Beatles record profits helped to pay for its research.
Ways of seeing inside the body, by debut.PET scan: It detects gamma rays from a radioactive sugar tracer, showing where tissue is active, not just what it looks like.
Ways of seeing inside the body, by debut.MRI of a human: Raymond Damadian's machine, nicknamed 'Indomitable', took about four hours to produce the first human full-body scan.
Ways of seeing inside the body, by debut.Functional MRI: It tracks blood-oxygen changes to show which brain areas are working, letting researchers watch thinking as it happens.
Ways of seeing inside the body, by debut.Swallowable pill camera: A capsule with a tiny camera, approved by the US FDA in 2001, films the gut as it travels through you, for around eight hours.

Founding of sports' governing bodies.MCC (cricket): The Marylebone Cricket Club, based at Lord's, wrote cricket's Laws and still looks after them today.
Founding of sports' governing bodies.The Football Association: Founded in a London tavern, it wrote the first common rules of football and is the sport's oldest association.
Founding of sports' governing bodies.International Rugby Board: Now called World Rugby, it began when Scotland, Ireland and Wales set it up; England joined a few years later.
Founding of sports' governing bodies.IOC: Pierre de Coubertin founded it in Paris, and the first modern Games followed in Athens just two years later.
Founding of sports' governing bodies.FIFA: Seven European nations founded it in Paris; its first World Cup took place in Uruguay in 1930.
Founding of sports' governing bodies.Imperial Cricket Conference: England, Australia and South Africa formed it, and it later grew into the International Cricket Council.
Founding of sports' governing bodies.IAAF (athletics): Founded in Stockholm during the Olympics there, it is now called World Athletics.
Founding of sports' governing bodies.FIDE (chess): Founded in Paris, its motto is 'Gens una sumus', meaning 'we are one family'.
Founding of sports' governing bodies.FIBA: Founded in Geneva, it saw basketball join the Olympic programme in Berlin four years later.
Founding of sports' governing bodies.UEFA: Formed in Basel, it runs the Champions League, whose forerunner the European Cup began the following year.

Sportswear brands, by founding year.New Balance: Founded in Boston making arch supports, it still manufactures some shoes in the United States.
Sportswear brands, by founding year.Converse: The Chuck Taylor All Star debuted as a basketball shoe in 1917, and hundreds of millions have been sold.
Sportswear brands, by founding year.Fila: It started in Biella, Italy, making underwear and knitwear, then became tennis fashion with Björn Borg.
Sportswear brands, by founding year.Champion: It invented the reverse-weave sweatshirt in the 1930s, designed to resist shrinking, and outfitted college teams.
Sportswear brands, by founding year.Puma: Rudolf Dassler founded it after a split with his brother Adi, who founded Adidas in the same Bavarian town of Herzogenaurach.
Sportswear brands, by founding year.Reebok (as Reebok): Joe Foster picked the name from the Afrikaans word for a type of African antelope, the grey rhebok.
Sportswear brands, by founding year.Vans: Paul Van Doren founded it in Anaheim, and its waffle sole grips skateboards.
Sportswear brands, by founding year.Nike (named Nike): The name honors the Greek goddess of victory; Phil Knight reportedly paid a student just $35 for the swoosh.
Sportswear brands, by founding year.Under Armour: Kevin Plank started it after tiring of sweat-soaked cotton shirts as a University of Maryland football player.
Sportswear brands, by founding year.Lululemon: Chip Wilson started it in Vancouver as a design studio by day and a yoga studio by night.

Where these scripts start in Unicode.Greek: Greek letters fill the block starting at U+0370, and scientists borrow them for everything from pi to alpha particles.
Where these scripts start in Unicode.Cyrillic: Cyrillic is used by Russian, Ukrainian, Bulgarian and many other languages, and it's named for St. Cyril.
Where these scripts start in Unicode.Armenian: The Armenian alphabet was created around 405 AD by Mesrop Mashtots, and its letters have barely changed.
Where these scripts start in Unicode.Hebrew: Hebrew is written right to left, and its block includes points that mark vowels.
Where these scripts start in Unicode.Arabic: Arabic is also written right to left, and its letters change shape depending on their position in a word.
Where these scripts start in Unicode.Devanagari: Devanagari is used for Hindi and Sanskrit, and its letters hang from a horizontal line.
Where these scripts start in Unicode.Thai: Thai script has no spaces between words, and its alphabet has 44 consonants.
Where these scripts start in Unicode.Georgian: Georgian has three different alphabets, and the modern one has no distinction between uppercase and lowercase.
Where these scripts start in Unicode.Hiragana: Hiragana is the Japanese syllabary used for grammar and native words, and it grew from cursive Chinese characters.
Where these scripts start in Unicode.Hangul syllables: Hangul syllables are built by combining letters into blocks, and this block holds over 11,000 of them.

Popes of the modern era, by election.Leo XIII: Reigned about 25 years, and his 1891 encyclical Rerum novarum spoke up for workers' rights; he lived to 93.
Popes of the modern era, by election.Pius X: Canonised in 1954, he was the first pope declared a saint in centuries, and reformed church music and liturgy.
Popes of the modern era, by election.Benedict XV: Elected weeks into World War I, he tried to broker peace, but both sides largely ignored his appeals.
Popes of the modern era, by election.Pius XI: He signed the Lateran Treaty of 1929 with Mussolini, which created Vatican City as an independent state.
Popes of the modern era, by election.Pius XII: He led the Church through World War II, and his wartime record is still debated by historians.
Popes of the modern era, by election.John XXIII: Elected at 76 as a 'caretaker', he surprised everyone by calling the Second Vatican Council.
Popes of the modern era, by election.Paul VI: The first modern pope to travel widely, visiting Jerusalem in 1964 and addressing the United Nations in 1965.
Popes of the modern era, by election.John Paul II: The first non-Italian pope in over four centuries, and one of the most travelled; he survived a 1981 shooting.
Popes of the modern era, by election.Benedict XVI: He resigned in 2013, the first pope in about 600 years to step down rather than die in office.
Popes of the modern era, by election.Francis: The first Jesuit pope and the first from the Americas, he took the name of Francis of Assisi.

Famous writers, by birth year.Geoffrey Chaucer: The medieval English poet wrote The Canterbury Tales, and he was among the first to be buried in Poets' Corner at Westminster Abbey.
Famous writers, by birth year.William Shakespeare: The playwright's name is spelled many different ways in documents, and he invented many words and phrases that are still used today.
Famous writers, by birth year.John Milton: The English poet wrote Paradise Lost after he went blind, and he dictated it to assistants.
Famous writers, by birth year.Jane Austen: The author of Pride and Prejudice published anonymously, and she described herself as 'by a Lady' on her title pages.
Famous writers, by birth year.Charles Dickens: The Victorian novelist wrote in instalments, and he gave the world Scrooge, and he wrote in the first person.
Famous writers, by birth year.Mark Twain: The writer, whose real name was Samuel Clemens, was born when Halley's Comet appeared, and he predicted that he would die when it returned.
Famous writers, by birth year.Virginia Woolf: The author of Mrs Dalloway helped lead the Bloomsbury Group, and she wrote that a woman needs money and a room of her own.
Famous writers, by birth year.Ernest Hemingway: The writer used short, plain sentences and he lived in Paris, Cuba and Key West, and won the Nobel Prize in 1954.
Famous writers, by birth year.Toni Morrison: The author of Beloved was the first African American woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 1993.
Famous writers, by birth year.J.K. Rowling: The author of Harry Potter wrote the first book in cafes in Edinburgh, and it was rejected by a dozen publishers.

Territories (not countries) by area.Gibraltar: The Rock of Gibraltar, British since 1713, is home to Europe's only wild monkeys, the Barbary macaques.
Territories (not countries) by area.Macau: Macau, Portuguese until 1999, has earned more from casino gambling than Las Vegas since 2006.
Territories (not countries) by area.Bermuda: Bermuda lies about 1,000 km off North Carolina, and is known for pink-sand beaches and Bermuda shorts worn to the office.
Territories (not countries) by area.Guam: Guam, a US territory in the western Pacific, lies near the Mariana Trench, the deepest part of Earth's oceans.
Territories (not countries) by area.Hong Kong: Hong Kong has more skyscrapers than any other city, with hundreds of buildings taller than 150 m.
Territories (not countries) by area.Faroe Islands: This self-governing part of Denmark may have a name meaning sheep islands, and sheep have long outnumbered people there.
Territories (not countries) by area.Puerto Rico: Puerto Ricans are US citizens, but residents of the territory cannot vote in presidential elections.
Territories (not countries) by area.Falkland Islands: Claimed by Argentina as the Malvinas, the Falklands were the scene of a 1982 war between Argentina and Britain.
Territories (not countries) by area.New Caledonia: New Caledonia is ringed by one of the world's largest lagoons and is home to crows that craft hooked tools from twigs.
Territories (not countries) by area.Greenland: Greenland is the world's largest island, and an ice sheet up to three kilometers thick covers about 80 percent of it.

How old are they?.The universe: The estimate comes from measuring the expansion rate and the cosmic microwave background.
How old are they?.The Sun: It is about halfway through its life as a hydrogen-burning star and will swell into a red giant in roughly five billion years.
How old are they?.The Moon: It most likely formed when a Mars-sized body called Theia crashed into the young Earth.
How old are they?.Earth's oldest zircon crystals: Found at Jack Hills in Western Australia, these tiny crystals suggest Earth had crust and probably oceans very early.
How old are they?.Acasta Gneiss (oldest rock): Found in Canada's Northwest Territories, it is the oldest known intact piece of Earth's crust.
How old are they?.Sirius: The brightest star in the night sky is far younger than the Sun, and has a white-dwarf companion.
How old are they?.The Pleiades: This 'Seven Sisters' cluster is visible to the naked eye, about 440 light-years away, and full of hot blue stars.
How old are they?.Betelgeuse: This red supergiant in Orion will eventually explode as a supernova, and it dimmed strangely in 2019–20.
How old are they?.Meteor Crater (Arizona): About 1.2 km wide, it was gouged by an iron meteorite and is among the best-preserved impact craters on Earth.
How old are they?.Crab Nebula: Chinese astronomers recorded the supernova in 1054, and its pulsar spins about 30 times a second.

Letter count of these famously long word.Hippopotamus: Greek for 'river horse', though it is more closely related to whales than horses.
Letter count of these famously long word.Sesquipedalian: Latin for 'a foot and a half long'. The Roman poet Horace used it to mock long-winded words.
Letter count of these famously long word.Uncopyrightable: One of the longest English words in which no letter repeats.
Letter count of these famously long word.Incomprehensibilities: Built by piling prefixes and suffixes onto 'comprehend', it shows how English can keep stretching words.
Letter count of these famously long word.Counterrevolutionaries: Describes people opposed to a revolution, a word that grew common after the French Revolution.
Letter count of these famously long word.Honorificabilitudinitatibus: It appears in Shakespeare's Love's Labour's Lost and means roughly 'the state of being loaded with honors'.
Letter count of these famously long word.Antidisestablishmentarianism: It first referred to 19th-century opposition to removing the Church of England's status as state church.
Letter count of these famously long word.Floccinaucinihilipilification: It means regarding something as worthless, and it is stitched together from Latin words for 'little value'.
Letter count of these famously long word.Supercalifragilistic…: Coined for the 1964 film Mary Poppins by the Sherman brothers, the full word is supercalifragilisticexpialidocious.
Letter count of these famously long word.Pneumonoultramicroscopic…: The full word is pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis, a made-up name for a lung disease from fine dust, famed as the longest in dictionaries.

G-forces, from free fall to rocket sled.Aboard the ISS: Astronauts aren't beyond gravity; at the station's altitude Earth's pull is still about 90 percent, but they are in continual free fall.
G-forces, from free fall to rocket sled.Moon's surface: Moon gravity is about a sixth of Earth's, which is why Apollo astronauts bounded along.
G-forces, from free fall to rocket sled.Mars's surface: On Mars you'd weigh only about 38 percent of your Earth weight, so you could jump much higher.
G-forces, from free fall to rocket sled.Earth's surface: One g is the acceleration of a falling object, about 9.8 metres per second faster each second.
G-forces, from free fall to rocket sled.Jupiter's cloud tops: Gravity at Jupiter's cloud tops is about two and a half times Earth's, the strongest among the planets.
G-forces, from free fall to rocket sled.Space Shuttle launch (max): Engines were throttled back so astronauts never felt much more than 3 g on ascent.
G-forces, from free fall to rocket sled.F1 car braking hard: F1 drivers feel around 5 g under braking, with similar sideways force in corners, so they train their neck muscles hard.
G-forces, from free fall to rocket sled.Fighter pilot's limit: Pilots wear g-suits and strain their muscles to keep blood in the brain, since near 9 g many would black out.
G-forces, from free fall to rocket sled.Sun's surface: The Sun's surface gravity is about 28 times Earth's, so a 70 kg person would weigh nearly two tons.
G-forces, from free fall to rocket sled.John Stapp's rocket sled: Air Force doctor John Stapp stopped from 632 mph in about a second and a half, proving humans can endure far more than assumed.

UK Poets Laureate, by year appointed.John Dryden: The first official laureate lost the post in 1689 after refusing to swear an oath to William III.
UK Poets Laureate, by year appointed.William Wordsworth: He accepted only after being assured he wouldn't have to write verse for royal occasions, and he wrote little as laureate.
UK Poets Laureate, by year appointed.Alfred Tennyson: He held the post for 42 years, longer than anyone, and wrote 'The Charge of the Light Brigade'.
UK Poets Laureate, by year appointed.Robert Bridges: A physician turned poet, he championed Gerard Manley Hopkins by publishing his poems posthumously in 1918.
UK Poets Laureate, by year appointed.John Masefield: A former sailor, he wrote 'Sea-Fever' (I must go down to the seas again) and stayed laureate for 37 years.
UK Poets Laureate, by year appointed.Cecil Day-Lewis: He also wrote detective novels as Nicholas Blake, and his son is actor Daniel Day-Lewis.
UK Poets Laureate, by year appointed.John Betjeman: Beloved for his light, humorous verse, he campaigned to save Victorian buildings like St Pancras station.
UK Poets Laureate, by year appointed.Ted Hughes: He was married to Sylvia Plath, and his animal poetry includes the collection Crow.
UK Poets Laureate, by year appointed.Andrew Motion: The first laureate appointed for a fixed ten-year term, instead of for life.
UK Poets Laureate, by year appointed.Carol Ann Duffy: The first woman, and first Scot, in the post.

Size it up: from credit card to bridge s.A credit card: Every bank card worldwide shares nearly identical dimensions, set by an international standard so they fit machines everywhere.
Size it up: from credit card to bridge s.An acoustic guitar: A guitar's hollow wooden body works as a resonating chamber, so strings can be heard without any amplifier.
Size it up: from credit card to bridge s.A giraffe (height): A giraffe has the same seven neck vertebrae as a human, though each one can be over 25 cm long.
Size it up: from credit card to bridge s.A double-decker bus: London's red double-deckers trace back to horse-drawn omnibuses, and early motor versions had open tops with no roof upstairs.
Size it up: from credit card to bridge s.A tennis court: The doubles court is wider than the singles one, which is why you see two sets of side lines on a tennis court.
Size it up: from credit card to bridge s.A blue whale: The largest animal known to have ever lived, it weighs well over 100 tonnes, and its heart is roughly the size of a small car.
Size it up: from credit card to bridge s.A Boeing 747: Nicknamed the Jumbo Jet, it got its hump so that the upper deck could be converted to cargo in case passenger flights lost out to supersonic ones.
Size it up: from credit card to bridge s.The Titanic: Struck an iceberg in 1912 on its maiden voyage, and its wreck lies 3.8 km down in the North Atlantic, first found in 1985.
Size it up: from credit card to bridge s.The Eiffel Tower (height): Built for the 1889 World's Fair, it was meant to stand only twenty years, and heat expansion makes it grow by roughly 15 cm in summer.
Size it up: from credit card to bridge s.Golden Gate Bridge main span: When it opened in 1937 it was the longest suspension span in the world, a title it held until 1964, and its color is called International Orange.

When these music technologies launched.Fairlight CMI sampler: This early sampler let musicians record real sounds and play them on a keyboard, and it shaped 1980s albums by Peter Gabriel and Kate Bush.
When these music technologies launched.MIDI standard: It lets instruments and computers from different makers talk to each other, and it is still used in almost every studio.
When these music technologies launched.Pro Tools: This recording software became the studio standard, and its name is a verb among audio engineers.
When these music technologies launched.Auto-Tune: Created by an engineer who earlier worked on seismic data for oil companies, it made Cher's "Believe" famous for its robotic vocal effect.
When these music technologies launched.Shazam: Launched in the UK, it first worked by dialing a number and holding the phone up to the music, and it replied with a text message.
When these music technologies launched.iTunes Store: It sold songs for 99 cents each, which helped turn around an industry that was reeling from file sharing.
When these music technologies launched.GarageBand: It came free with new Macs, and let amateurs make loops and songs with no studio experience.
When these music technologies launched.Pandora radio: It built its playlists with the Music Genome Project, where analysts rated songs on hundreds of musical traits.
When these music technologies launched.SoundCloud: The Berlin-based platform became a launchpad for unsigned artists and gave rise to the "SoundCloud rap" scene.
When these music technologies launched.Apple Music: It launched with a live radio station called Beats 1, after Apple had bought the headphone company Beats.

Web standards by year.HTML 2.0: HTML 2.0 was the first formally standardised HTML, published as an IETF document in 1995. The earlier 'HTML 1' was never an official standard.
Web standards by year.HTTP/1.1: It made persistent connections the default, so many files could share one link. This version stayed the web's workhorse for about two decades.
Web standards by year.XML 1.0: XML was a streamlined version of the older SGML, built to let any field define its own tags while staying readable by people and machines.
Web standards by year.XHTML 1.0: It recast HTML as strict XML, but the web never loved its rigidity, and HTML5 later won out instead.
Web standards by year.The term AJAX: Jesse James Garrett coined the term in an essay, naming the trick that made Gmail and Google Maps update without reloading the page.
Web standards by year.ECMAScript 5: It followed a long gap after version 3 in 1999, after a bigger fourth version was abandoned. It added strict mode and native JSON support.
Web standards by year.JSON as ECMA-404: Douglas Crockford popularised the format, and says he discovered it rather than invented it, since it was already valid JavaScript.
Web standards by year.JavaScript arrow functions: The => syntax arrived with the 2015 JavaScript update, and arrow functions also inherit 'this' from their surroundings.
Web standards by year.WebAssembly (W3C standard): It became the fourth language natively understood by browsers, after HTML, CSS and JavaScript, letting near-native code run on a page.
Web standards by year.HTTP/3: HTTP/3 runs over QUIC on UDP instead of TCP, so one lost packet no longer stalls every other file on the page.

Keeping time: when these arrived.Egyptian shadow clock: A bar's moving shadow marked the time, and it was designed to be turned around at midday to face the other way.
Keeping time: when these arrived.Mechanical clock: The earliest ones had no dial, but struck bells, and the word 'clock' comes from a medieval word for bell.
Keeping time: when these arrived.Henlein's pocket watch: Peter Henlein of Nuremberg is credited with a small spring-powered watch, nicknamed a 'Nuremberg egg'.
Keeping time: when these arrived.Huygens' pendulum clock: Christiaan Huygens's clock cut errors from minutes a day to about a quarter minute, transforming timekeeping.
Keeping time: when these arrived.Patek Philippe wristwatch: Patek Philippe made a wristwatch for Hungarian Countess Koscowicz, one of the earliest known, when watches were thought women's jewellery.
Keeping time: when these arrived.US railroad time zones: On 18 November, called 'the day of two noons', US railways adopted standard time zones to replace hundreds of local times.
Keeping time: when these arrived.Daylight saving (Germany): Germany was the first country to adopt daylight saving, in World War I, to save coal.
Keeping time: when these arrived.Quartz clock: Warren Marrison at Bell Labs built it, using a vibrating crystal that kept time far better than pendulums.
Keeping time: when these arrived.Caesium atomic clock: Today the second is defined by caesium atoms vibrating 9,192,631,770 times; the first working clock was built at Britain's NPL.
Keeping time: when these arrived.Quartz wristwatch: Seiko's Astron was the first quartz wristwatch on sale, and it led to the inexpensive digital watch boom.

When these foods were invented.The sandwich (Earl's legend): Legend says the Earl asked for meat between bread so he could keep playing cards without greasy fingers.
When these foods were invented.Potato chips: A popular tale credits chef George Crum, who sliced potatoes extra thin to spite a complaining customer, though the story is disputed.
When these foods were invented.Corn flakes: The Kellogg brothers' cereal began with a lucky accident: wheat left sitting got flaky when rolled out.
When these foods were invented.Cotton candy machine: It was invented by a dentist, William Morrison, and a confectioner, John Wharton, and debuted at the 1904 World's Fair.
When these foods were invented.Popsicle: It was invented by Frank Epperson, then 11, who left a soda with a stirring stick out on a cold night.
When these foods were invented.Sliced bread: Otto Rohwedder's Missouri bakery machine gave us the saying 'the best thing since sliced bread'.
When these foods were invented.Chocolate chip cookie: Ruth Wakefield created it at the Toll House Inn in Massachusetts, adding chopped chocolate to a butter cookie.
When these foods were invented.TV dinner: Swanson launched it in 1953, and it's often said to have been a way to use up a huge surplus of turkey.
When these foods were invented.Instant noodles: Momofuku Ando's creation was flash-fried noodles you could cook in minutes, and he's called one of Japan's greatest inventors.
When these foods were invented.Lunchables: Oscar Mayer launched the kit as 'Lunch Combinations', with crackers, meat and cheese in a tray.

When these gadgets first went on sale.Polaroid instant camera: Edwin Land's camera produced a finished print in about a minute; he said the idea came when his young daughter asked why she couldn't see the photo now.
When these gadgets first went on sale.Regency TR-1 transistor radio: The first commercially made transistor radio sold for about $50 and fit in a pocket, which helped make rock and roll portable.
When these gadgets first went on sale.Sony Walkman: Sony's cassette player went on sale in Japan in 1979; abroad it first carried names like Soundabout and Stowaway before Walkman stuck.
When these gadgets first went on sale.IBM PC: IBM built it from off-the-shelf parts and Microsoft's DOS, which invited a wave of clones and shaped personal computing for decades.
When these gadgets first went on sale.Motorola DynaTAC phone: Martin Cooper placed the first handheld cell call in 1973; the commercial DynaTAC took a decade to reach shops, weighed nearly a kilo and cost about $4,000.
When these gadgets first went on sale.Tamagotchi: Bandai's egg-shaped virtual pet from Japan needed constant feeding and care, and could die if neglected; tens of millions were sold.
When these gadgets first went on sale.BlackBerry: Its tiny thumb keyboard and push email made it so habit-forming that people nicknamed it the CrackBerry.
When these gadgets first went on sale.Amazon Kindle: It sold out in about five and a half hours at $399 in late 2007, and Amazon couldn't restock until the following spring.
When these gadgets first went on sale.Amazon Echo: Amazon's voice-controlled speaker introduced Alexa to homes; it launched quietly, available first by invitation to Prime members.
When these gadgets first went on sale.Oculus Quest: Its release in May 2019 made it the first mainstream standalone VR headset, with no PC or cables needed to play.

Best Picture Oscar winners, by ceremony.Casablanca: The script was still being written during filming, and nobody knew how it would end.
Best Picture Oscar winners, by ceremony.The Godfather: Marlon Brando declined his Best Actor Oscar and sent Sacheen Littlefeather to protest on his behalf.
Best Picture Oscar winners, by ceremony.Rocky: Sylvester Stallone wrote the script in a few days and refused to sell it unless he could play the lead.
Best Picture Oscar winners, by ceremony.Rain Man: Dustin Hoffman researched his role with Kim Peek, a savant who inspired the character.
Best Picture Oscar winners, by ceremony.Forrest Gump: Tom Hanks won his second consecutive Best Actor Oscar, after Philadelphia, for the role.
Best Picture Oscar winners, by ceremony.Titanic: It won 11 Oscars, tying the record set by Ben-Hur.
Best Picture Oscar winners, by ceremony.Gladiator: Oliver Reed died during filming, so his remaining scenes were completed with digital effects.
Best Picture Oscar winners, by ceremony.The Departed: Martin Scorsese won his first Best Director Oscar for this remake of the Hong Kong thriller Infernal Affairs.
Best Picture Oscar winners, by ceremony.Slumdog Millionaire: Danny Boyle shot it in Mumbai, and composer A. R. Rahman won two Oscars for it.
Best Picture Oscar winners, by ceremony.Parasite: It became the first non-English-language film to win Best Picture, directed by Bong Joon-ho.

Healers through history, by birth year.Hippocrates: The Greek 'father of medicine'. The 'do no harm' line many people attribute to his oath does not actually appear in it.
Healers through history, by birth year.Galen: A Greek physician to gladiators and emperors. His animal-based anatomy ruled European medicine for about 1,400 years.
Healers through history, by birth year.Avicenna: The Persian polymath Ibn Sina wrote The Canon of Medicine, a standard textbook in both Europe and the Islamic world for centuries.
Healers through history, by birth year.Paracelsus: The Swiss physician who declared 'the dose makes the poison', a founding idea of toxicology, and championed chemicals as medicine.
Healers through history, by birth year.William Harvey: Showed in 1628 that the heart pumps blood in a circuit around the body, overturning ideas that had stood since Galen.
Healers through history, by birth year.Edward Jenner: A country doctor who used cowpox to protect against smallpox in 1796. 'Vaccine' comes from the Latin word for cow, vacca.
Healers through history, by birth year.Florence Nightingale: The 'Lady with the Lamp' of the Crimean War was also a statistician who invented a polar-area chart to show disease deaths.
Healers through history, by birth year.Sigmund Freud: Founder of psychoanalysis, born in what is now Czechia. His 'unconscious' and 'Freudian slip' entered everyday speech.
Healers through history, by birth year.Alexander Fleming: In 1928 he noticed that mould on a neglected dish killed bacteria. That led to penicillin and a share of the 1945 Nobel Prize.
Healers through history, by birth year.Jonas Salk: His polio vaccine was declared safe in 1955. Asked who owned the patent, he reportedly said, 'Could you patent the sun?'

Hebrew letters by their numeric (gematri.ב Bet: Bet means 'house', and the Torah starts with this letter, in the word for 'in the beginning'.
Hebrew letters by their numeric (gematri.ה He: According to Genesis, God added this letter to Abram's name, making him Abraham, and also to Sarai, making Sarah.
Hebrew letters by their numeric (gematri.י Yod: The smallest letter, a tiny stroke; some scholars think the 'jot' in 'jot or tittle' refers to it.
Hebrew letters by their numeric (gematri.כ Kaf: The name means the 'palm' of the hand, and the letter takes a different shape, ך, at the end of a word.
Hebrew letters by their numeric (gematri.מ Mem: Its name is the Hebrew word for 'water', and it has a closed final form ם that appears at word endings.
Hebrew letters by their numeric (gematri.ס Samekh: A rounded, closed letter with no final form; its name is thought to mean 'support' or 'prop' in Hebrew.
Hebrew letters by their numeric (gematri.צ Tsadi: It resembles the word tzaddik, 'righteous person', and has a final form ץ used at the end of words.
Hebrew letters by their numeric (gematri.ק Qof: Its name resembles the modern Hebrew word for 'monkey', though the letter's origin may be linked to the back of the head.
Hebrew letters by their numeric (gematri.ש Shin: Shin appears on mezuzah cases, standing for Shaddai, a name of God, and it is also the first letter of 'shalom'.
Hebrew letters by their numeric (gematri.ת Tav: The last letter, whose name means 'mark'; the phrase 'from alef to tav' is Hebrew for 'from A to Z'.

A chick's life, from egg to hen.Hen lays an egg: A hen needs about 25 hours to make an egg, and a good layer produces nearly one a day. The shell is mostly calcium carbonate.
A chick's life, from egg to hen.Hen sits on it to keep warm: A broody hen turns her eggs several times a day to keep the embryo from sticking to the shell. She leaves the nest only briefly to eat and drink.
A chick's life, from egg to hen.Chick grows for three weeks: It takes about 21 days to hatch. After only a few days, a tiny heart is already beating, visible when a farmer shines a light through the shell.
A chick's life, from egg to hen.Pokes into the air pocket: Between the shell membranes there is an air cell, and the chick breathes from it for the first time before it breaks through. This is called internal pipping.
A chick's life, from egg to hen.Cracks a hole in the shell: The chick uses a small hard bump on its beak, the egg tooth, to chip around the shell. This can take many hours of effort.
A chick's life, from egg to hen.Hatches wet and tired: Hatching is exhausting, and the chick rests often. It emerges damp and exhausted after as much as a day of work in the shell.
A chick's life, from egg to hen.Dries into fluff: Within hours the damp chick dries into soft down. It can eat and walk almost immediately, as chicks are precocial.
A chick's life, from egg to hen.Grows real feathers: By a few weeks old, proper feathers replace the fluffy down. Chicks grow fast, and reach adult size in months.
A chick's life, from egg to hen.Becomes a young pullet: A female chicken under a year old is a pullet. Young males are called cockerels, and begin to develop combs and wattles.
A chick's life, from egg to hen.Lays her first egg: Hens start laying at about five to six months old. The first eggs are usually small, and sometimes lack a yolk.

Elvis Presley's life, in order.Born in Tupelo: He was born in a small two-room house in Mississippi; his twin brother Jesse Garon was stillborn, a loss Elvis spoke of throughout his life.
Elvis Presley's life, in order.First single at Sun Records: That's All Right, recorded in Memphis with Scotty Moore and Bill Black, blended blues and country into the sound producer Sam Phillips had been hunting for.
Elvis Presley's life, in order.\"Heartbreak Hotel\": His first US number one was inspired by a newspaper story about a man who left a suicide note reading, I walk a lonely street.
Elvis Presley's life, in order.Drafted into the Army: He served as an ordinary soldier rather than taking an easy entertainment posting, and in West Germany he met Priscilla Beaulieu.
Elvis Presley's life, in order.Leaves the Army: Back from Germany as a sergeant, he went straight to a television welcome-home special hosted by Frank Sinatra, and then to new records.
Elvis Presley's life, in order.Marries Priscilla: The small ceremony took place in Las Vegas and lasted only minutes; their daughter Lisa Marie was born nine months later.
Elvis Presley's life, in order.'68 Comeback Special: Dressed in black leather and performing in the round on NBC, he revived a career that had been drifting through weak movies.
Elvis Presley's life, in order.Aloha from Hawaii: Broadcast by satellite to much of Asia and beyond, it reached an audience estimated in the hundreds of millions, and the album went to number one.
Elvis Presley's life, in order.Dies at Graceland: He died at 42 at his Memphis mansion, and fans still gather outside every August for a candlelight vigil.
Elvis Presley's life, in order.Graceland opens to visitors: Just five years after his death the mansion opened its doors, and it has become one of the most visited private homes in the United States.

Christmas movies, by release year.It's a Wonderful Life: A box office disappointment at first, it became a holiday classic after its copyright lapsed and TV stations aired it constantly.
Christmas movies, by release year.Miracle on 34th Street: The film used the real Macy's Thanksgiving Parade as a backdrop, and it won an Oscar for Edmund Gwenn as Kris Kringle.
Christmas movies, by release year.White Christmas: Named for the Irving Berlin song, the movie was Paramount's top moneymaker of its year and starred Bing Crosby.
Christmas movies, by release year.A Charlie Brown Christmas: Network executives doubted it, with its jazz score and no laugh track, but it won an Emmy and airs yearly.
Christmas movies, by release year.Die Hard: Whether it's a Christmas movie is an annual debate, but it's set on Christmas Eve at an office party in Los Angeles.
Christmas movies, by release year.Christmas Vacation: Chevy Chase plays Clark Griswold, who covers his house with 25,000 lights, and it was the third film in the Vacation series.
Christmas movies, by release year.Home Alone: It became the highest-grossing live-action comedy of its time and made young Macaulay Culkin a huge star.
Christmas movies, by release year.The Santa Clause: Tim Allen plays a man who takes over from Santa after an accident on the roof, one of the better-known holiday comedies of the 1990s.
Christmas movies, by release year.Elf: Will Ferrell's Buddy was raised at the North Pole, and the movie uses real forced-perspective sets rather than digital effects for its elf scenes.
Christmas movies, by release year.The Polar Express: It was among the first feature films made entirely with motion capture, with Tom Hanks playing several roles.
